facts.status_note: Listed as gone; no source describes what, if anything, remains at the site

Three lightning fires burned over 80 acres on a Sunday evening, as reported in a July 30, 1941 newspaper; first fire reported from the new station

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com lists a camp in 1935, and Idaho Fire Lookouts gives the same entry, but the 1941 newspaper accounts describe a lookout station being planned in April and set up by late July. The record dates the station to 1941 and keeps the 1935 camp as a separate event with no further detail.
The 1941 newspapers name the Minidoka National Forest; firelookout.com names the Sawtooth National Forest. Both names are kept.

notes_for_editor: All 1941, 1960 and 1961 detail comes from newspaper clippings transcribed on Forest Lookouts; the original newspapers were not opened. The 1935 camp date on firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts is unexplained and conflicts with the 1941 accounts. The 1960 entry says Pike peak; Forest Lookouts lists it on the Pike Mountain page, so it is assumed to be this site. No access level set because no source states one. Sawtooth vs Minidoka naming is a name change or an error; the sources do not say which. No photos added.
